newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Arboyne says Glencore to sell Nonoc nickel.
newsitem.headline: Arboyne says Glencore to sell Nonoc nickel.

text.p: Swiss-based commodites trader Glencore International AG will act as sales agent for nickel and cobalt produced at the Nonoc mine complex in the Phillipines under a five year agreement, Arboyne Ltd said on Thursday.
The agreement also will see Glencore purhcase at pre-set prices all material not sold to third parties, Arboyne said.
Arboyne in July 1996 entered into an agreement to take over and recommission the Nonoc complex, which has been closed since 1986.
Nonoc, which was brought to closure by high debt, low metals prices and a depressed Philippine peso, is capable of producing up to 65 million pounds of metal a year.
The five year agreement was reached between Glencore and Philinco Mining and Industrial Group, which is acquiring Nonoc from the Philippine government through Pacific Holdings Ltd.
Perth-based Arboyne, listed on the Australian Stock Exchange, holds an option to acquire Pacific Holdings.
Arboyne finance director Simon Boadle said the agreement also calls for Glencore to help Nonoc re-register its nickel as deliverable to the London Metal Exchange.
Glencore earlier this year reached a sales agreement covering the sales of nickel produced from the Murrin Murrin mine in Western Australia proposed by Anaconda Nickel ltd .
